transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Rita Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (CTO, Centris), Luis Romero (Head of Infra), Hannah Cho (Security Lead), Samir Jain (Platform Eng)

Summary (auto):
Centris is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive clinical NLP tasks. Primary asks: strict tenant isolation for PHI-adjacent workloads, predictable reserved GPU capacity, and short high-frequency burst handling for read-heavy inference. Security checklist and cost/latency tradeoffs are blockers. Next step: pricing, burst model sims, and SOC2/KMS alignment.

Topics: Dedicated reservation options, isolation/topology, warm pools/pre-warm, burst throttling and billing, VPC/private plane and KMS, latency SLOs, rollout/canary strategy.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you squeezing this in. quick intro from our side — Maya is our systems SE who owns dedicated infra, Rita is on CSM.
[00:08] Priya (CTO): Thanks — we are excited. quick context: Centris runs clinical summarization and de-ident pipelines. some models touch PHI tokens; others are strictly de-id. goal is low latency for live clinician queries, but also big nightly batches.
[00:22] Luis (Head of Infra): We want a reserved GPU footprint because spiky traffic on M-F mornings has broken a few of our hosted POCs. also need strong tenancy isolation — can't have noisy neighbors touching cert data.
[00:35] Maya (SE): Great, that maps well to Redwood Dedicated. our reserved pools give you isolation at the node level; you can opt for tenant-fenced nodes (single-tenant) or shared nodes with strict cgroup isolation. question for you — what percent of inference is latency-critical vs batch?
[00:48] Priya: Roughly 65% low-latency interactive, maybe 35% batch overnight. latency SLO for the interactive path is 200ms p50 and we'd like to be under 350ms p95 for the main clinician flow.
[01:05] Maya: Ok that helps. what model families are you using? are these open Llama variants or larger commercial models?
[01:12] Samir (Platform Eng): We're mostly on a fine-tuned Llama-2-13B variant for summarization, and a smaller 7B for routing/intent detection. we're experimenting with quantization but haven't committed yet.
[01:24] Maya: Nice, 13B is a good fit for dedicated GPU pools. on 13B we typically see [inaudible] reduced ops with int8 / q4_x formats; that affects throughput and memory. for your p95 targets with a 13B we can model prewarmed KV caches and small batch sizes.
[01:40] Luis: Prewarmed caches — can you explain operationally what that means? we had bad warm-up tails previously where the first few requests were slow because model kv cache not populated.
[01:49] Maya: Sure — we do two things: warm-pool nodes kept with model loaded and KV cache primed for common prefixes, and short-lived prewarm on scale-up. warm pools cost a bit but cut tail latency. you can tune warm-pool size and prewarm thresholds so you only pay for what you need.
[02:06] Hannah (Security): On the security front — we need to understand where keys live. does Redwood Dedicated support customer-managed KMS/HSM? and audit log retention?
[02:15] Jared: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS (bring-your-own) and you can get audit logs for inference requests, model access, and admin ops — retention tiers are configurable. we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs.
[02:28] Hannah: also SSO / SAML for console access and RBAC for different teams?
[02:33] Rita (CSM): Yep, SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC are standard on Dedicated; plus we can set IP allowlists on the console and webhook endpoints.
[02:42] Priya: Important: any PHI touching logs — we need encryption at rest and in transit and the ability to disable analytics on those requests.
[02:51] Maya: Understood. we have options to disable telemetry on specified routes and to route PHI-inference to private-only deployment lanes.
[02:58] Samir: On bursting — mornings we see 4x baseline for 20–30 minutes with short spikes up to 10x for 2–3 minutes. what are the pricing and behavior for burst? do we get throttled?
[03:10] Jared: Good question. Dedicated includes reserved baseline capacity; we offer burst pools (shared across customers) and priority burst for Dedicated customers depending on contract. we can model cost both as on-demand + reserved blended or as committed tiers with defined burst credits. there are also warm-pool strategies to avoid cold starts during spikes.
[03:28] Maya: From an ops POV, we recommend a hybrid: reserve enough nodes for p50/p95 typical load, keep a small warm pool for quick bursts, and enable soft-burst fallback to hosted variants in other regions if you want more headroom. fallback comes with routing latency and egress considerations.
[03:44] Luis: Fallback to hosted variants — is that allowed with PHI?
[03:49] Maya: Not by default. if PHI-sensitive, you'd route to Private-only or to another dedicated pool that you've reserved in another region. we can support cross-region Dedicated failover under an enterprise contract but that requires data residency signoffs.
[04:02] Priya: So cost modeling — we need an example: say steady 10 rps, 4x morning burst to 40 rps for 25 minutes, 10x 3-minute spikes twice a day. can you share what that looks like as cost change for reserved vs reserved+burst?
[04:18] Jared: We'll put together a spreadsheet; Maya can simulate token-level compute and memory. generally you pay for reserved node uptime plus burst premiums when you exceed reservation. options: larger reservation to cut burst premiums, or smaller reservation + burst credits. we'll show both.
[04:31] Maya: One caveat — for your 13B and p95 requirements, you might want to reserve slightly more cores for headroom to avoid queueing. also batching helps cost but can add latency; so small batch sizes (1–4) are more typical for interactive.
[04:46] Hannah: Auditability — do you provide request-level logs with hashing so we can prove no raw PHI was persisted? also need delete capabilities for a given date range.
[04:58] Jared: Yes, request-level logs are available; we can redact payloads or hash them on ingestion before storing. deletion APIs exist, and we can coordinate retention with your security team.
[05:10] Priya: What about canary deploys and model version pinning? we want a safe rollout when we push a new fine-tune.
[05:16] Maya: Redwood supports model pins and canary rollouts — you can split traffic e.g., 95/5 and automatically fallback to previous model on error rates. there are built-in eval hooks to run a small set of canary prompts against the new model before it receives production traffic.
[05:30] Samir: Network egress — our security team needs private control plane and VPC peering. is console control plane ever in the public network?
[05:37] Jared: For Dedicated we offer a private control plane option that sits within your VPC and uses private peering for control signals; the management plane can be VPC-restricted. full on-prem is also an option for air-gapped setups.
[05:48] Luis: Nice. what's the typical lead time to get a dedicated pool up and warmed?
[05:52] Maya: Depends on procurement and commit. if we're using our hosted region hardware, typical provision + model warm is 3–7 business days; on-prem or specialized HSM setups add 2–4 weeks.
[05:59] Priya: Our procurement window is tight; we'd like a 30–45 day SLA from PO to go-live. doable?
[06:06] Jared: For enterprise contracts we can often hit that if paperwork is prioritized. we'll coordinate legal and procurement.
[06:12] Hannah: Encryption in transit — are we TLS 1.2/1.3 and is mTLS supported for internal service-to-service?
[06:17] Maya: TLS 1.2+ and mTLS supported for inter-service; customer-managed certs are supported on Dedicated.
[06:24] Priya: Any known limitations with quantization? our models sometimes lose subtle clinical phrasing.
[06:30] Maya: Yes quantization can impact delicate medical phrasing. we typically recommend A/B evals: q4 on less-sensitive routes; keep full precision for critical summarization. Redwood Optimize offers quality regression alerts tied to your prompt set so you can detect drift after quantizing.
[06:46] Luis: For the burst scenario — can we pre-allocate ephemeral nodes for known bursts (like 08:00–08:30) and only pay for those windows?
[06:54] Maya: We support scheduled pre-warms and time-bound ephemeral allocation; billing can be per-minute. that hybrid pattern is common for predictable daily surges.
[07:03] Priya: Are there guardrails to prevent runaway cost for spikes due to a bug?
[07:08] Jared: Yes, you can set budget caps and circuit breakers — e.g., limit burst to N concurrent nodes, or drop to a lower-cost model variant if costs exceed thresholds. alerts and automatic rollback are available.
[07:19] Samir: For testing we'd like a pilot for one week to validate latencies and failovers. can we get a small reserved pool for that?
[07:25] Jared: absolutely. our standard pilot is a 2–4 node reserved pool for 7–14 days with telemetry. pricing is often waived or discounted.
[07:33] Priya: Good. on the security paperwork, you'll need a data processing addendum and proof of SOC2.
[07:40] Rita: we'll email the DPA template and SOC2 docs after the call.
[07:45] Hannah: Also, can you confirm roles who get console access? we need audit trails for who flips model pins.
[07:52] Maya: RBAC can map to your SAML groups, and every admin action is logged with user identity and IP.
[08:00] Jared: Quick recap of deliverables — I'll send a cost model spreadsheet with reservation vs reserved+burst scenarios, Maya will run a sim against your sample traces for latency/cost, and Rita will share SOC2/DPA and a pilot agreement template.
[08:15] Priya: Sounds good. timeline — we'll aim to review the pricing + sim by next Friday; procurement will start after that.
[08:23] Jared: Great. anything else?
[08:26] Luis: One more: do you have any references in healthcare that ran similar live inference with PHI constraints?
[08:32] Jared: We can provide anonymized references and a short case study — we'll include that with the follow-up email.
[08:38] Priya: That's it from us — thanks.
[08:40] Jared: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the technical deep dive.
